messages:
maria: Quick note: onboarding sample app hit an SSE resume bug. After a network flap some JSON messages are arriving with duplicated or missing tail fragments, causing parsers to fail. Repro steps below.

ben: Browser EventSource or node stream?

maria: Both. EventSource in browser sample and node-fetch in node sample. Steps: 1) start a multi-chunk JSON stream 2) simulate flaky network mid-message 3) reconnect using Last-Event-ID and sometimes see duplicated fragments or a missing suffix.

sam: Sounds like resume token semantics: the server may be advancing last-event-id at fragment emission, not at logical-message completion. Any console trace?

maria: Example trace from browser console: 
received chunk id=1 data="{"text":"Hello"}"
received chunk id=2 data="{"text":"Wo"
// drop here
reconnect Last-Event-ID=2
received chunk id=2 data="rld"
received chunk id=3 data="{"text":"Bye"}"

maria: That leads to either duplicate assembly of id=2 or interleaving with id=3. Python sample buffers until newline so it's fine; Go sample parses per chunk and breaks. Mobile sees worst behavior.

ben: Short-term: add defensive reassembly in sample apps. Maintain a small last-fragment hash per event id and drop duplicates on resume. Add a README note in quickstart.

sam: Long-term: runtime should publish resume tokens at logical-message boundaries or emit a sentinel comment when a full message is flushed (e.g., ":boundary <token>"). File a ticket with traces.

maria: Filed TKT-3412: "streaming: make resume tokens map to logical message boundaries" with attached logs. Pushed small patch: event-id buffering + dedupe in browser/node samples and a headless test that simulates flaps.

ben: Reviewed. Add inline comment explaining the dedupe hack and an env flag to run the network-flap test locally.

ci-bot: CI passed: sample-app tests (branch: fix/sse-resume) :white_check_mark:

maria: Thanks. Marking this for follow-up when runtime change is planned. :thumbsup:
